subject: Label separate runs as disease/control to create diagnosis for class comparison

messages.author: 71755fba910dfee9
messages.subject: Label separate runs as disease/control to create diagnosis for class comparison
parts:
Hi everyone,

Kylie thanks again for a great package, I am enjoying using it! 

I apologise if this is a basic question, but I was wondering if anyone could help me with setting a diagnosis. I've read the rcc vignette and looked at the other questions on this forum. I understand how to set the diagnosis based on pixel location (as in the rcc vignette) or based on a classifying m/z using selectROI.

However, I have a dataset where each sample is a separate run (imzML file). I have used combine to combine the datasets, and now want to set the diagnosis so I can do statistical analysis. Does anyone have a suggestion of how to do this? I assume I can use the run information since that has the name of each sample?

Thanks in advance, I'm a newbie with R so appreciate this google group and everyone's helpful advice!

Cheers,
Sandra

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: Label separate runs as disease/control to create diagnosis for class comparison
parts:
Hi Sandra,

I annotate my single files before combining them to make sure that in whatever combination I later re-use or combine them I always have the annotations ready.

In your case, you are right, you can re-use the run information if it corresponds to your diagnosis:

diagnosis <- makeFactor("diagnosis1" = run(mse)=="run1", "diagnosis2" = run(mse)=="run2") ## you can add more diagnoses in case you have more than two
## you can either use this vector or attach it to the MSI data make sure that you keep the right annotations during your following analysis:
pData(mse)$diagnosis <- diagnosis

Hope that helps,
Melanie
